mainText: This is Dose of Good for Monday, November 9. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Brazilian university creates 3D-printing resin for heart devices that doesn't clot. Tested on an artificial heart prototype under 4 cm, the Unicamp resin formed no clots in the lab, releases nitric oxide and let blood-vessel cells grow on it. The team has already patented it. Second: Nature is being restored in 149 countries, creating over 1 million green jobs. A UN report counts 252 million hectares of ecosystems under restoration. Brazil has 3.4 million hectares, and jaguars are coming back. Third: 12,300 favelas get postcodes, giving 16 million people a recognised address. Brazil's CEP para Todos program gave at least one postcode to every favela mapped by the IBGE. Street-level codes come next. Fourth: Rottweiler rescued in critical condition recovers and finds a home. Nevoeiro went through rehabilitation with trainer Marcela Barbieri and was adopted by Carlos, who never gave up on him. Fifth: Open platform shares 15,900 Brazilian genomes to improve diagnoses. Brazil's Genomas SUS program released data on 15,900 complete genomes and 3.7 million genetic variants, helping doctors diagnose diseases in the Brazilian population. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
